analysis.title: Americas Clean Technology: Solar: RE+ preview, NXT capital markets day also in focus as sector looks to pivot post-232/midterms
key_insights: GS previews RE+ (Las Vegas, Nov 16-19), the largest N.A. solar/storage trade show, and expects investor focus on 2027/2028 demand, recent utility-scale bookings, resi demand recovery, and policy after the US midterms.

Solar coverage is down 34% YTD against +14% for the R2K. GS attributes this to Section 232 polysilicon uncertainty plus higher rates, fears that a data center slowdown cuts demand, and continued resi weakness. FLNC operational issues and management changes added idiosyncratic damage. The group has improved over the past month, particularly after the midterms.

GS prefers Buy-rated NXT (on Conviction List) and FSLR in utility-scale and Buy-rated ENPH in residential. ENPH is favored for margins and balance sheet that should insulate it from near-term market weakness.
GS expects US utility-scale solar demand to stay relatively stable through 2029 despite higher solar pricing after the Section 232 polysilicon outcome and elevated rates.

Resi: GS forecasts a contraction in 2026, +10% yoy in 2027, then +5% in both 2028 and 2029. Higher-for-longer rates could bias the 2027 view lower. Rising utility rates, easier comps and better financing availability (tax equity, prepaid leases) support the recovery.

Supply and demand: GS estimates global module capacity utilization at 47% for 2026E and 48% for 2027E. Polysilicon and module prices are subdued for now, but the Section 232 outcome could lift US panel prices to an implied $0.44/w from $0.30-0.35/w today. China polysilicon price laws and possible joint production cuts are another upside risk to prices, with uncertain impact.

Policy: 45X is the key sector-specific lever for US solar manufacturers, and 45Y/48E remains important for project timing and economics. Investors will look for the size and timing of polysilicon-driven price increases and how much can be passed through.

New products should get more attention at RE+, notably solid-state transformers (SSTs) tied to 800 VDC data center power architectures. RE+ hosts an 800 VDC Data Center Demonstration with 13 participants including ABB and ENPH. Other products in focus are SEDG's Nexis, ENPH's G5 battery and SHLS' AirLink and storage.
NXT holds a Capital Markets Day on Nov 16 at 3pm PST, one year after the CMD that set FY2030 targets. GS sees it as a near-term catalyst and expects an upgrade to long-term targets.

NXT's FY2030 targets from the 2025 CMD are revenue of $4.8-5.6bn, adj. EBITDA of $1.1-1.3bn and FCF of $0.8-1.0bn. GS thinks management could raise these to revenue of $6.2-7.0bn, adj. EBITDA of $1.4-1.6bn and FCF of $1.0-1.2bn. The midpoint would capture consensus (FY30 revenue $6.66bn, adj. EBITDA $1.493bn).

The NXT upside rests on closed acquisitions (Apex Power, Prevalon, Zimmermann PV-Steel), which GS estimates add over $1bn of FY2030 revenue, and on management saying as early as its F1Q27 call that it was trending above the initial targets.

Other NXT CMD items: color on FY2028 demand (not given on the F2Q27 call, and the market fears a steep drop from contract delays or restructuring after Section 232), possible segment disclosure (battery storage, core trackers, other), a likely data center customer example, and margins. GS flags possible margin compression from acquired businesses.
GS sensitivity on NXT FY2029: each 50bp move in margins moves adj. EPS by $0.11 and adj. EBITDA by $21mn, while a 1% move in opex moves adj. EPS by $0.04 and adj. EBITDA by $7mn.

GS hosts RE+ meetings with RUN, SEDG, ARRY, Ohm Analytics, ENPH, SHLS, OKLO, GameChange Energy, NXT and Lunar Energy. Recurring questions cover bookings and demand into 2027/2028, Section 232 effects on contracting, 45X extension in 2027, SST milestones and storage traction, and 25D restoration for resi.

Ratings and 12-month targets: Buy FSLR $272, NXT $127, RUN $13, ENPH $40. Neutral FLNC $7, HASI $43. Sell SEDG $25, CSIQ $10, JKS $7, NRGV $3.25. ARRY and SHLS are Not Rated because GS is acting as financial advisor in a strategic matter involving them.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and on the Conviction List. GS sees the Nov 16 CMD as a near-term catalyst with upside to FY2030 revenue, adj. EBITDA and FCF targets.
Favored in utility-scale to benefit from strong demand and higher ASPs after the Section 232 polysilicon outcome.
Preferred in resi for strong margins and balance sheet, with growth drivers from new products and end markets.
Buy-rated resi name valued on NAV. Risks are slower MW growth, policy shifts and higher rates.
Operational issues and management changes drove steep underperformance (-73% YTD). Risks include Houston ramp delays.
Valued on P/B plus dividend yield. Sensitive to rates and policy.
Sell-rated. Upside risks are better inverter ASPs, favorable policy and falling rates.
Sell-rated on EV/EBITDA and SOTP. Risks are faster module ASP recovery and favorable policy.
Sell-rated on EV/EBITDA. Risks are faster cost declines and lower poly pricing.
Target history lists $3.25 on 11-Nov-26, up from $3.00 on 12-Aug-26. Sell-rated on EV/Sales plus EV/EBITDA.

sector_views.rationale: Constructive. Demand should stay relatively stable through 2029 and NXT and FSLR benefit from strong demand and higher ASPs.
Expected +10% yoy in 2027 and +5% in 2028 and 2029, still below historic levels, with downward risk if rates stay high. ENPH preferred.

earnings_insights: NXT GS forecasts (not reported): FY27 revenue $4,377mn and adj. EBITDA $937mn, FY28 revenue $5,204mn and adj. EBITDA $1,145mn, FY29 revenue $5,947mn and adj. EBITDA $1,349mn against FY29 consensus of $5,958mn and $1,334mn.
NXT adj. EBITDA margin: GS forecasts 21.4% for FY27, 22.0% for FY28 and 22.7% for FY29 against FY29 consensus of 22.4%. FY30 consensus is revenue $6,660mn, adj. EBITDA $1,493mn and margin 22.4%.
NXT GS FCF forecasts: $516mn FY27, $688mn FY28, $905mn FY29. The 2025 CMD FCF target for FY2030 was $800-1,000mn, and GS's possible revised target is $1,000-1,200mn.

NXT 2025 CMD FY2030 targets (company guidance, Nov 12, 2025): revenue $4.8-5.6bn (about 12% CAGR from FY2025), midpoint split of $3.6bn trackers, $0.9bn foundations/frames, $0.5bn electrical/EBOS and $250mn software. Non-tracker revenue was to rise to about one third of the total from about 13% in FY2026.

NXT acquisitions: Apex Power closed 7/30/26 (GS forecasts $115mn revenue in FY2029), Prevalon closed 7/20/26 (about $333mn revenue run rate at acquisition, GS forecasts $408mn in FY2029), and Zimmermann PV-Steel Group closed after F2Q27 (about $343mn run rate). GS estimates over $1bn combined FY2030 revenue.
NXT management said as early as its F1Q27 earnings call that it was trending above its initial FY2030 targets, and it gave no FY2028 view on its F2Q27 call.

NXT FY2029 GS sensitivity (illustrative): each 50bp of margin is $0.11 of adj. EPS and $21mn of adj. EBITDA (30bp of adj. EBITDA margin). A 1% move in opex is $0.04 of EPS and $7mn of adj. EBITDA (10bp).

macro_indicators.indicator: Implied US solar module price after Section 232 polysilicon outcome
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects higher US panel prices after the polysilicon tariff outcome, which would raise project costs and test how much can be passed through. Supports FSLR ASPs.
Depressed but stable utilization means oversupply persists and input prices stay subdued, though near-term risk is to the upside.
Slow recovery from easier comps, rising utility rates and better financing, with downward bias if rates stay higher for longer.
Underlying demand persists despite higher module pricing and elevated interest rates.

trade_ideas.description: Long Buy-rated NXT (Conviction List) ahead of Nov 16 Capital Markets Day, on expected raise of FY2030 revenue, adj. EBITDA and FCF targets
trade_ideas.rationale: Acquisitions and management's comments on trending above targets point to upward revisions that would also capture consensus at the midpoint.
trade_ideas.risk: Increasing competition, customer attrition, patent protection, market demand, policy, and supplier product availability/pricing.

trade_ideas.description: Long Buy-rated FSLR as a utility-scale solar beneficiary of strong demand and higher ASPs
trade_ideas.rationale: Section 232 polysilicon outcome should push US panel prices higher while utility-scale demand stays stable.
trade_ideas.risk: Module oversupply, higher than expected module costs, trade policy, changes to US manufacturing credits.

trade_ideas.description: Long Buy-rated ENPH as the preferred residential solar name
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong margins and balance sheet insulate it against near-term market weakness while new products and end markets drive growth.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower-than-expected market growth, market share losses, lower-than-anticipated ASPs, higher power costs, lower ex. US growth.

risk_factors: Section 232 polysilicon outcome raising panel prices and causing contract delays or restructuring that could hit FY2028 demand.
Higher interest rates for longer hurting project economics and resi customer value proposition.
Slowdown in data center development weighing on solar demand.
Continued weakness in the residential market and uncertain macro.
NXT margin compression as acquired businesses are integrated.
Uncertainty over 45X tax credit changes and whether 25D credits could be restored.
Uncertain impact of China polysilicon price laws and joint production cuts.
Company-specific operational issues such as FLNC's Houston ramp delays and management changes.

Exhibit 2: Upside/downside to GS price targets as of 11/10/2026. FSLR 50%, ENPH 46%, FLNC 42%, RUN 41%, NXT 26%, HASI 12%, CSIQ 0%, SEDG -5%, NRGV -13%, JKS -31%.
Exhibit 8: NXT FY27-FY30 GS and consensus revenue, adj. EBITDA, margin and FCF versus the 2025 CMD targets and the potentially revised FY30 targets.
Exhibits 9 and 10: NXT FY29 adj. EPS and adj. EBITDA sensitivity grids to changes in COGS (-1.5% to +1.5%) and opex (-3% to +3%), with the base adj. EBITDA at $1,349mn.
geopolitical: Section 232 trade action outcome on polysilicon, expected to raise US solar panel prices.
China polysilicon price laws and possible joint production cuts that could lift polysilicon prices.
US midterm election results and their implications for solar policy, 45X manufacturing credits, 25D resi credits and 45Y/48E.
